author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest reveals a lesser known piece of history, Victory Gardens during World War One and Two were so productive that after the war ended, the US government actually urged people to stop growing their own food, fearing it would hurt American agriculture and cost returning soldiers their jobs. He connects that same instinct to today, arguing that real freedom means communities that are food and energy independent, not reliant on Big Egg, Bill Gates, or centralized systems that thrive on keeping people dependent. It's a compelling case for self sufficiency as both a practical and spiritual act of reclaiming personal agency.

description:
Russell reflects on the death of Professor Jason Arday, who faced relentless public scrutiny over claims about his biography and academic work before his passing. Drawing on his own experience of being investigated by the same publication, Russell speaks candidly about the toll public shaming can take, and urges people not to let outrage on either extreme cloud their judgment.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell dives into the growing movement to break free from the two party system, spotlighting the staggering fact that independents now outnumber both Democrats and Republicans combined. A former Ralph Nader campaign coordinator lays out just how stacked the odds are against independent candidates, needing nearly a million signatures compared to a fraction of that for major party candidates. Russell closes with a sharp analogy about the illusion of choice, comparing it to letting a child pick between two options while the outcome stays exactly the same either way.
